title: CodeRefinery-työpaja
content:
Are you writing code and managing data for your research? Do you spend too much time on tedious manual tasks? Struggling to understand and reuse your own or others’ older code?

Join the CodeRefinery workshop September 22-24 and 29 – October 1, 2026, 11 – 16 EEST (Helsinki time), for free and online.

  • Version control with git with focus on collaboration and not only for the command line 
  • Reproducibility: Preparing code to be usable by you and others in the future 
  • What can you do to get credit for your code and to allow reuse 
  • How to document your research software
  • Responsible use of generative AI in assisted coding 
  • Preventing yourself and others from breaking your functioning code 
  • Modular code development: Making reusing parts of your code easier

    • This hands-on workshop introduces tools and techniques to help you write more FAIR (Findable, Accessible, Interoperable, Reusable) research code. It is not a course to learn programming.

    The workshop will be most beneficial if you already have programming experience in any language.

  • For a detailed list of prerequisites to ensure the best experience, please visit the CodeRefinery workshop page.

    • The workshop is free and open to everyone.

title: EOSC Finnish Forum webinar: RDA Plenary 27 and EOSC Symposium 2026 highlights
content:
October is a busy month! The 27th RDA Plenary takes place in London 6th-8th October, and the annual EOSC Symposium meets in Florence, 14th-16th October. At this EOSC Finnish Forum webinar, we will hear from CSC's RDA organisational assembly representative Anu Märkälä (CSC) on this year's highlights, and from EOSC Finland representative Ulriika Vihervalli (CSC) on what to expect from the EOSC Symposium. Come along to learn the latest on RDA and EOSC developments – the webinar will help you assess if participating in London and/or Florence is worth your and your organisation's while.

The webinar presentation materials are here and the recording is here.

Agenda

  • 5' Introduction
  • 15' RDA Plenary 27 highlights (Anu Märkälä, CSC)
  • 15' EOSC Symposium 2026: highlights and key developments (Ulriika Vihervalli, CSC)
  • 10' Q&A-osio

title: Avoimen tieteen ja tutkimuksen talvipäivät 2026
content:
The Open Science and Research Winter Conference will take place on 16–17 November 2026 at the Finnish Meteorological Institute in Helsinki. The event is organised by the Finnish Meteorological Institute and the Open Science and Research Coordination. The theme of the 2026 Winter Days is “From Open to Operational.” The event will be held in a hybrid format. The Languages of the event will be English and Finnish.

  • Register via form until 2.11.

    • Open science has moved beyond principles and policies. The challenge today is no longer whether science should be open, but how openness can be transformed into real scientific, societal and economic impact. This year’s winter conference explores how to bridge the gap between vision and implementation, turning open science into an operational reality.

    The event consists of keynote presentations and thematic sessions, where short presentations are combined with interactive discussion between the audience and the speakers. Thematic sessions will include researchers views to what are the bottlenecks of open science, exploring the promises of AI to research and interoperable open science ecosystems and processes, not forgetting the northern lights.

title: CAM Together! Online Roundtable on Career Assessment Matrices as tools to support responsible researcher assessment
content:
The Federation of Finnish Learned Societies, the University of Turku and Lapland University of Applied Sciences invite you to an online roundtable exploring career assessment matrices and their role in supporting responsible researcher assessment on 31 August, 13:00–15:00 CEST (14:00–16:00 Finnish time/EEST). The webinar will be held in English.

Register to the webinar here.

Registration is open until 21 August 2026. Registered participants will receive a link closer to the event.

Career assessment matrices (CAM) are practical tools that help organisations assess researchers in a more holistic, fair and transparent way. Rather than focusing primarily on publications and quantitative indicators, career assessment matrices recognise a broad range of researchers' contributions and competencies.

During the event, speakers from Finland, Sweden and Norway will share how career assessment matrices are being developed and used in their national contexts. Through presentations and discussion, participants will gain insights into how these tools can support the implementation of responsible researcher assessment.

title: EOSC Finnish Forumin data-avaruuswebinaari
content:
You are warmly invited to this webinar hosted by EOSC Finnish Forum on data spaces. In the webinar, we will hear from three experts: Hanna Nurmi-Hugaerts (TIEKE) will introduce the concept and discuss work being done in Finland, Pihla Kauranen will discuss data spaces from an EOSC perspective, and Heidi Laine (CSC) will discuss data spaces and data labs for the LUMI AI Factory.

Come along to learn the latest on data spaces development! The session will be held in English, and there will be time at the end for a Q&A.

We kindly ask you to register through this link.

Agenda:

  • 5´ Welcome
  • 15´ Hanna Nurmi-Hugaerts (TIEKE): Data Spaces in Practice: Concept, Use Case examples and Collaboration in Finland
  • 15´ Pihla Kauranen (CSC): Data Spaces and EOSC
  • 15´ Heidi Laine (CSC): Data for AI - LUMI AI Factory, Data Labs, and Data Spaces
  • 10´ Q&A

    • For any queries, please contact: eosc-ff-support(at)postit.csc.fi

title: Capacity Building workshop for Citizen Science -työpaja
content:
What parts of the research can be opened to public? Join for a half day in person citizen science themed workshop 27 February 9.30-13 (EET) in English with experts from Aarhus University, University of Turku and the national Open Science coordination. Learn the basics, share your experience or test your project idea with peers.

Workshop is a warm-up event for the European Citizen Science Association annual conference ECSA 2026 in Oulu 3-6 March and organized with the support of the PATTERN-project  and Helsinki University Library.

  • Register via form by 19 February 

    • The workshop takes place in the University of Helsinki City Centre Campus Fabianinkatu 26 Language centre 115. The room is accessible.

    9:30 Coffee and introductions

    10:00 Welcoming remarks with Jonni Karlsson, AVOTT

    10:15 Fundamental principles with Gitte Kragh, AU

    10:45 Case: Herizo Andrianandrasana, UH: Community-based Conservation in Madagascar

    11:15 Short break

    11:30 Participant Recruitment and Community Engagement with Gitte Kragh, AU

    12:00 Case: Sanni Helander, UTU: Science belongs to everyone! Developing participatory science

    12:30 Discussion, closing remarks
